thesis: World's largest publicly traded copper producer at the epicenter of electrification, grid buildout, and AI data-center power demand — copper prices sit at record highs on a structural supply deficit. Q2 2026 beat handily (adjusted EPS $0.74 vs $0.62; revenue $7.03B) with U.S. operations net income up 65% YoY. The Grasberg Block Cave ramp is progressing on schedule after the prior operational disruption, and a new Indonesia agreement extends key asset lifespans, reducing the long-standing regulatory overhang. Investment-grade balance sheet with no significant 2026 debt maturities backs continued dividends and performance-based returns.

drivers: Copper holds at record highs on a widening structural deficit (electrification, grid, AI data centers)
Grasberg Block Cave ramp exceeds plan; smelting fully restored
Leach initiative reaches ~300M lb/yr run-rate at low capital intensity
Copper sales scale to 3.8B lbs (2027) and 4.1B lbs (2028) per guidance
Multiple analyst target raises (Barclays $82, RBC $73, Wells Fargo $70) prove conservative

base_case.assumptions: Copper stays firm but off peak; Grasberg ramps as guided; Indonesia terms hold under the new agreement; FY2026 copper sales ~3.1B lbs and gold ~0.65M oz; capex ~$4.3B; steady 3-4% copper demand growth.

risks: Copper corrects on global recession or a deeper China property slowdown
Grasberg ramp stalls or a fresh operational disruption emerges
Indonesia imposes punitive export/permitting terms despite the new MoU
Rising capex and unit costs compress margins
AI/electrification demand narrative disappoints near term

catalysts.event: Q3 2026 earnings — production, unit costs, and updated 2026 guidance
Grasberg Block Cave ramp milestones and restoration of full mining/smelting operations
Copper price and LME inventory moves — leverage to the structural deficit
Indonesia terms and permitting under the new asset-life-extension agreement
Leach initiative progress toward a ~300M lb/yr copper run-rate

key_risks: Indonesia political/regulatory risk — government majority stakeholder via Inalum; export and permitting exposure remains despite the new agreement
Commodity price volatility — heavy revenue sensitivity to copper prices
Grasberg operational execution — Block Cave ramp complexity after the prior disruption
China demand slowdown — roughly 40% of global copper demand
Rising capex (~$4.3B FY2026) and unit-cost inflation
ESG and tailings/water management risks across mining operations
